mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-8.7 to -12.3). This autocorrelated downward momentum in discretionary shopping and recreation behavior is expected to persist, producing a lower mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the prior 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell monotonically from -8.7 to -12.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite the three-week prior decline, indicating momentum does not persist.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility crossed from strongly positive (+20.3) to negative (-8.0) within four weeks, a signature of newly imposed outdoor-gathering restrictions. Once PARKS crosses zero, similar restriction tightening typically spreads to retail settings, pulling RETAIL_REC further down over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from positive to negative week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 20.3 to -8.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises in the two weeks after PARKS turns negative, showing no transmission from parks restriction to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT (-17.7 to -22.3) and WORKPLACES (-13.6 to -12.1, with a trough at -22.7) jointly suppress the daytime foot-traffic pipeline that feeds retail corridors. When both commuting-related series are depressed together, the compounded reduction in people moving through transit hubs and office districts depresses RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain deeply negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain jointly depressed, falsifying the compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has risen steadily (2.7 to 4.0) while the region is in a tightening-restrictions regime (evidenced by collapsing PARKS and TRANSIT). In this regime, rising RESIDENTIAL reflects increased stay-at-home compliance, which mechanically reduces discretionary outings and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.7 to 4.0 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise, indicating the stay-at-home linkage does not hold in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline from +20.3 to -8.0 over four weeks is consistent with a seasonal transition (e.g., end of favorable outdoor weather or holiday period) rather than policy action. This seasonal pullback in outdoor activity is expected to coincide with, and lead, a short-term seasonal dampening of nearby retail foot traffic within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell by nearly 28 points over the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following the steep PARKS decline, suggesting the PARKS drop is policy-driven rather than seasonal.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable and mildly elevated (9.3 to 11.9) throughout the snapshot while RETAIL_REC fell, suggesting households have already substituted discretionary retail trips for essential-goods trips. Once this substitution saturates (GROCERY_PHARM plateaus), pent-up discretionary demand is expected to produce a rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change stays within +/-1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM varied only between 9.3 and 11.9 across four weeks while RETAIL_REC fell steadily
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline even after GROCERY_PHARM plateaus, rejecting the substitution-saturation rebound mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT drop exceeding 15 points (as seen between t-3w and t-2w, -17.7 to -21.6) signals an acute reduction in cross-town mobility that directly removes transit-dependent shoppers from retail districts within the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -17.7 to -21.6 between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 15 points, indicating no short-horizon transit-to-retail linkage.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility shows a volatile V-shape (-13.6, -22.7, -12.1, -12.1) consistent with policy flip-flopping (partial office reopenings followed by re-closures). When WORKPLACES volatility is high and co-occurs with falling TRANSIT, uncertainty about commuting policy suppresses planned retail trips linked to commute routines, producing a net RETAIL_REC decline over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung from -13.6 to -22.7 then back to -12.1 within the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks despite continued WORKPLACES volatility and TRANSIT decline, rejecting the uncertainty-suppression interaction.
